messages:
maria: Quick design check — TL;DR: for long console forms (create-pool, project settings) do we prefer inline errors + contextual highlights, or a persistent side summary that anchors to the right? Also want to revisit destructive confirms: typed-confirm vs a lighter pattern (checkbox + undo toast). alex: leaning inline for immediate fixes, side summary for long pages where multiple fields can fail at once. side summary helps users scan all issues after submit. :point_right: leah: +1 for hybrid. Inline for field-level validation on blur, side summary after a failed submit. We tried pure inline and users missed errors above the fold. sam: Accessibility note — whatever we pick needs clear aria-live behavior. If we only use inline messages, screen readers won't easily discover summary of multiple errors. We should assertively announce top-level summary on submit failure. Example we used before: ```
\n 3 errors prevented saving. Press tab to jump to first error.\n
``` jordan: For required markers — can we stop default asterisk-only? It confuses product folks. Proposal: show explicit "Required" helper text for critical fields and soft asterisk for others. Keeps visual clutter down but clearer in tests. maria: That sounds reasonable. We also need to think about color contrast on asterisks and not rely on color alone for required state. alex: On typed-confirm for deletes: typed confirm reduces accidents but is slow for power users. Proposed compromise: for high-impact deletes (tenant-level, permanent data) use typed-confirm; for medium-impact (single pool) we do checkbox + a 10s undo toast + prominent danger styling. leah: usability test note — participants preferred typed-confirm in concept but hated typing long names. Short typed pattern (type the word "DELETE") worked well. Also keyboard focus should land in the input. sam: technical nit: typed-confirm must be reachable by assistive tech — input should have aria-label and we should avoid custom JS-only widgets. Also ensure that the undo toast is focusable and announced. jordan: Copy suggestions for summary header: instead of "There are errors", use "We couldn't save — 3 issues to fix". More actionable. maria: Good. Also propose the side summary include 1) short header with count, 2) list of errors with clickable anchors (jump to field), 3) collapsible details for error tips. That way it's compact but scannable. alex: small CSS/behavior ask: when jumping from summary to inline field focus that field and expose the inline message (don't hide it behind collapsed section). Also animate scroll to reduce context loss. leah: Implementation sketch for linking: anchor links with data-focus-target and on click: focus() + add `aria-describedby` to the input to include the inline error id. We need to avoid layout shifts. aria-bot: deploy-preview available at https://staging.redwood.ai/console/forms/validation-v2 — uses side-summary hybrid + typed-confirm toggle on settings page. maria: Next steps: alex to draft component API (SideErrorSummary), leah to write accessibility checklist, sam to add aria-live test to E2E. Jordan will run a 5-person guerrilla test on Monday. I'll consolidate copy suggestions in the doc. :thumbsup: alex: I'll post a quick PR with the component props by EOD. maria: Thanks everyone — this feels like a clear path forward.
